description:
The Distribution of Kerosene Oil Scheme is a significant welfare initiative launched by the Government of India to ensure the availability of kerosene oil to the economically weaker sections of society. 

The scheme was first introduced in 1970 as part of the Public Distribution System. 

It aims to provide subsidized kerosene oil to households that do not have access to alternative sources of energy. 

The primary objective of the scheme is to ensure that low-income families can afford kerosene for cooking and lighting purposes. 

The government recognizes that many rural and urban poor households rely on kerosene oil due to the lack of access to electricity and other cooking fuels. 

As of 2023, the scheme covers approximately 1.2 crore beneficiaries across various states in India. 

The kerosene is provided at a subsidized rate to eligible households. 

The subsidy is aimed at reducing the financial burden on low-income families. 

Under this scheme, kerosene is distributed through the Public Distribution System. 

The government allocates a specific quantity of kerosene oil to each eligible household. 

Typically, each household can receive up to 5 liters of kerosene oil per month. 

The price of kerosene oil under this scheme is set at INR 32 per liter. 

This is significantly lower than the market price, which can be as high as INR 70 per liter in some regions. 

The scheme is implemented by the Ministry of Consumer Affairs Food and Public Distribution. 

State governments are responsible for the actual distribution of kerosene oil to the beneficiaries. 

Eligibility for the Distribution of Kerosene Oil Scheme is primarily based on economic status. 

Households that fall below the poverty line are given priority in the allocation of kerosene oil. 

The criteria for determining eligibility include income limits set by the government. 

For example, families with a monthly income of less than INR 10,000 are generally eligible. 

Additionally, households that do not have access to electricity or other cooking fuels are also prioritized. 

The application process for the scheme involves several steps. 

Eligible households must apply through their local ration shops or designated government offices. 

They need to provide specific documents to prove their eligibility. 

These documents typically include proof of identity such as an Aadhaar card or voter ID. 

Proof of residence is also required, which can be a utility bill or a rental agreement. 

Income certificates issued by local authorities are necessary to confirm the economic status of the household. 

Once the application is submitted, it is verified by the concerned authorities. 

After verification, eligible households are issued a ration card that includes details about the kerosene allocation. 

The distribution of kerosene oil occurs on a monthly basis. 

Beneficiaries can collect their allocated kerosene from designated ration shops. 

The distribution schedule is usually fixed by the state governments. 

In some states, beneficiaries are notified through SMS or local announcements regarding the distribution dates. 

The kerosene oil is stored in government-approved depots before being distributed to the ration shops. 

The implementing authorities for the scheme include the Food and Civil Supplies Departments of various state governments. 

Each state has its own contact details for the respective departments. 

For instance, in Maharashtra, beneficiaries can contact the Food and Civil Supplies Department at 1800 222 202. 

In Tamil Nadu, the contact number is 1800 425 5901. 

The scheme has seen various revisions and improvements since its inception. 

In 2013, the government introduced the National Food Security Act. 

This act aimed to provide legal entitlement to subsidized food grains and also included provisions for kerosene distribution. 

The act mandates that the government must ensure the availability of kerosene to eligible households. 

As of 2023, the government has allocated approximately 1.5 million kiloliters of kerosene oil for distribution under this scheme. 

This allocation is reviewed annually based on the number of beneficiaries and consumption patterns. 

The scheme also aims to promote the use of cleaner fuels over kerosene oil. 

In recent years, the government has been encouraging the adoption of liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) as a cooking fuel. 

Subsidies for LPG connections have been provided to further reduce dependency on kerosene oil. 

Despite these efforts, kerosene remains a crucial energy source for many households in India. 

The Distribution of Kerosene Oil Scheme plays a vital role in ensuring energy security for the poorest sections of society. 

The government continues to monitor and evaluate the scheme to enhance its effectiveness. 

Feedback from beneficiaries is collected to improve the distribution process. 

The scheme is also subject to audits to ensure transparency and accountability. 

In conclusion, the Distribution of Kerosene Oil Scheme is an essential welfare initiative. 

It provides subsidized kerosene oil to low-income households. 

The scheme aims to alleviate the financial burden of energy costs. 

It also strives to ensure that no household is left without a reliable source of energy for cooking and lighting. 

With ongoing efforts to improve the scheme, the government remains committed to supporting the needs of the economically weaker sections of society.
